design_summary: FPGA-synthesizable supervisory controller for adaptive aero control with firmware-visible MMIO, bounded external model request/response transport, response validation, timeout supervision, command limiting, and actuator-valid inhibition on invalid or stale conditions.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level supervisory controller and firmware-visible MMIO wrapper for adaptive aero control. Implements register decode, command sequencing, request formatting, response validation, timeout supervision, stale-data detection, command limiting, and safety inhibition of actuator-valid when a request cannot be validated or is not permitted. The module exposes a 64-bit MMIO register window and two 128-bit transport channels for external model request/response packets.
top_module.functionality: Implements the complete firmware control plane and external model transport contract for an adaptive aero controller. MMIO writes configure control, timeout threshold, actuator min/max limits, rate-limit setting, request tag/sequence behavior, and fault clear behavior. A write to control.start launches a new request when idle. A write to control.abort immediately cancels the outstanding transaction and inhibits actuator_valid. The request formatter produces a bounded 128-bit request packet with version, sequence tag, length metadata, serialized vehicle/flow metadata, and checksum/parity. The response validator checks framing, response length, expected transaction tag, and freshness against the active request and timeout watchdog. Any invalid, stale, malformed, missing, or late response causes actuator output validity to remain deasserted and faults to latch for firmware handling. Actuator commands are clamped to configured min/max bounds and optionally rate-limited before being presented at actuator_command; actuator_valid is asserted only after successful validation and limiting. Status and debug counters are readable through MMIO and are synchronized to the internal controller state.
responsibilities: Expose firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control and status interface.
Launch and abort bounded transport transactions.
Format request packets for the external surrogate service.
Validate response packets against tag, length, freshness, and timeout rules.
Clamp and optionally rate-limit actuator commands.
Deassert actuator_valid on reset, invalid response, timeout, or host disable.
Latch faults until cleared by dedicated MMIO clear register or reset.
Expose debug counters for accepted, rejected, timeout, and clamp events.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, all state resets synchronously to a safe inactive condition. mmio_ready may assert to permit access after reset release, but actuator_valid must be deasserted, req_valid deasserted, rsp_ready deasserted until the controller is ready to accept a response, busy cleared, fault_code cleared or reset-defined, and all debug counters cleared. The controller shall not silently substitute a commanded output on reset; actuator validity remains deasserted until a new start transaction is accepted and a valid response is received and applied.
behavior_rules: MMIO register decode must be synchronous and must implement every documented register field.
The request packet must include explicit version, sequence, length, and checksum/parity metadata.
req_valid may assert only when a request packet is fully formed and the controller is not busy with a prior outstanding request.
req_last shall mark the final beat of the bounded request packet; if the implementation uses a single beat, req_last shall assert with req_valid.
rsp_ready shall be asserted only while the controller can accept a response for the current outstanding request.
Any response whose tag does not match the outstanding sequence, whose length is inconsistent, or whose framing is malformed shall be rejected and latched as a fault.
Responses received after the configured timeout threshold shall be rejected as stale/timeout and shall not update actuator_command or actuator_valid.
Actuator command limiting shall clamp the final command to configured min/max bounds and apply the configured rate limit if enabled.
actuator_valid shall assert only after validation succeeds and command limiting completes.
A host write to control.abort shall immediately cancel the transaction, deassert actuator_valid, and latch the abort fault.
Faults shall remain latched until explicit MMIO clear or reset.
If the host disables closed-loop operation, the controller shall inhibit actuator_valid and refuse to launch new transactions until re-enabled.
No combinational loop may exist between request/response handshakes and actuator outputs.
The controller shall not emit an uninitialized or stale actuator command.

modules.name: request_formatter
modules.description: Packages host-provided serialized vehicle and flow-condition metadata into a bounded 128-bit outbound request packet for the external surrogate service. Adds version, sequence tag, payload length, and checksum/parity metadata, and presents a ready/valid handshake toward the request transport path.
modules.functionality: Encodes a single bounded request beat or a bounded multi-beat request packet, depending on implementation choice, with explicit framing metadata. The formatter must not perform any physics computation; it only serializes the minimal semantic inputs required by the external service. Packet integrity fields such as version, sequence, length, and checksum/parity are inserted here.
responsibilities: Serialize request metadata into a 128-bit transport packet.
Insert version, sequence, and length metadata.
Generate req_valid_out/req_last_out only when a packet is ready and downstream ready is observed.
Emit request_accepted to inform the controller that the request launch has been accepted by the transport stage.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, request outputs deassert and packet contents are cleared to a known state.
behavior_rules: The formatter shall not expose geometry arrays, tensors, or flow fields.
The formatter shall not generate requests when format_enable is deasserted.
The formatter shall use only the provided metadata inputs and shall not infer hidden state from transport outputs.
Packet checksum/parity, if used, must be bounded and deterministic.

modules.name: response_validator
modules.description: Validates the bounded 128-bit response stream from the external surrogate service against the current outstanding request tag, response length, framing, and freshness rules. Produces semantic response validity and rejection reasons for the top-level safety sequencer.
modules.functionality: Checks response validity, tag match, packet framing, and freshness. Extracts a bounded 32-bit command recommendation from the response payload only after validation. Invalid, stale, or late packets are rejected and flagged; no command is forwarded unless the packet is valid and timely.
responsibilities: Validate response framing and length consistency.
Compare response tag to the expected outstanding request tag.
Reject stale or timeout-expired responses.
Extract a bounded 32-bit command recommendation only from validated payload fields.
Raise reason flags for malformed, sequence-mismatch, or stale responses.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, all validation outputs deassert and validated_command_out clears to a known value.
behavior_rules: The validator shall not accept a response for any tag other than the active outstanding request tag.
The validator shall not forward a command from a malformed or late response.
If timeout_expired_in is asserted, the response shall be treated as stale and rejected.
Response payload contents are treated as opaque except for the minimal fields needed for validation and command extraction.

modules.name: actuator_command_limiter
modules.description: Applies clamp and optional rate-limiting to validated actuator commands before presentation at the top-level actuator output. All command values are constrained to configured min and max bounds before use. The limiter only processes commands when commanded by the top-level controller state.
modules.functionality: Clamps the input command to configured bounds and optionally rate-limits changes between updates. Reports whether any clamping occurred. Does not assert actuator validity; that decision is owned by the top-level safety sequencer.
responsibilities: Clamp commands to configured min/max bounds.
Optionally apply bounded rate limiting.
Indicate whether the command was clamped.
Keep behavior deterministic and FPGA-friendly.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, command_out returns to a known value and command_clamped_out deasserts.
behavior_rules: Clamping shall be applied whenever apply_in is asserted.
The limiter shall never bypass configured min/max bounds.
Rate limiting, if enabled, shall preserve boundedness.
The limiter shall not infer or generate fallback actuation; it only constrains provided commands.

modules.name: stale_data_monitor
modules.description: Tracks request age, outstanding sequence tag, and freshness conditions for the active transaction. Generates timeout and stale indicators used by the controller and response validator.
modules.functionality: Maintains watchdog state for the currently outstanding request and asserts freshness/timeout indicators. Provides the active sequence tag and busy indication to surrounding control logic.
responsibilities: Measure request age against configured timeout threshold.
Track outstanding request sequence tag.
Assert timeout and stale indicators when appropriate.
Support abort and start sequencing without combinational loops.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, busy clears, timeout and stale flags clear, and the current sequence tag resets to a known value.
behavior_rules: A response arriving after timeout threshold is stale.
An abort immediately clears the outstanding request context.
The monitor shall not create a response acceptance path; it only observes and reports freshness state.

modules.name: mmio_register_block
modules.description: Implements the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface and decodes the full register map into semantic control, configuration, and status fields. Provides only real, reachable registers; no inaccessible software-visible state is declared. All registers are synchronous and readable/writable according to the contract.
modules.functionality: Decodes a 64-bit register window with control, status, fault, counters, sequence seed, timeout threshold, actuator min/max limits, rate-limit setting, last-request tag, last-response tag, and safe-state configuration. Write strobes and byte enables are supported through mmio_wstrb. control.start begins a transaction when idle. control.abort cancels the current transaction. control.clear_faults clears latched faults. Readbacks return the currently committed configuration and live status/counters.
responsibilities: Provide firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decode.
Implement the exact register map described in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract.
Expose writable configuration registers and readable status/counter registers.
Generate semantic control pulses for start, abort, enable, and clear faults.
Return registered read data through mmio_rdata and transaction-ready semantics through mmio_ready.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, writable configuration registers load safe defaults, control pulses deassert, and read data returns a defined reset value. Latched fault presentation follows reset-clear semantics.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
No register may be presented as software-visible unless it is actually implemented and readable/writable as specified.
MMIO decode shall be synchronous and shall not create combinational loops with transport or actuator outputs.
Byte enables from mmio_wstrb shall be honored if implemented.
The block shall expose the full register contract required by firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: control_start
inter_module_signals.description: MMIO start pulse that initiates a new request transaction when idle.

inter_module_signals.name: control_abort
inter_module_signals.description: MMIO abort pulse that cancels the outstanding transaction.

inter_module_signals.name: control_enable
inter_module_signals.description: Host enable/closed-loop control forwarded to the request formatter.

inter_module_signals.name: timeout_threshold_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Configured timeout threshold forwarded to the watchdog monitor.

inter_module_signals.name: sequence_seed_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Sequence seed or next request tag used by the formatter and monitor.

inter_module_signals.name: actuator_min_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Minimum actuator command bound.

inter_module_signals.name: actuator_max_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Maximum actuator command bound.

inter_module_signals.name: rate_limit_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Optional rate-limit step setting for the limiter.

inter_module_signals.name: safe_state_cfg
inter_module_signals.description: Safe-state or serialized payload length/configuration metadata consumed by the formatter as part of bounded request packaging.

inter_module_signals.name: request_accepted
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates the request packet has been accepted for transmission and the watchdog should consider the transaction active.

inter_module_signals.name: timeout_expired_out
inter_module_signals.description: Watchdog timeout indication into the validator and register block.

inter_module_signals.name: busy_out
inter_module_signals.description: Busy status into the response validator and register block.

inter_module_signals.name: response_valid_out
inter_module_signals.description: Validated response indicator to firmware status logic.

inter_module_signals.name: response_stale_out
inter_module_signals.description: Stale-response status back to firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: malformed_response_out
inter_module_signals.description: Malformed-response status back to firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: sequence_error_out
inter_module_signals.description: Sequence error status back to firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: validated_command_out
inter_module_signals.description: Validated command recommendation forwarded into the limiter.

inter_module_signals.name: limit_enable_in
inter_module_signals.description: Enable gate for the command limiter.

inter_module_signals.name: apply_in
inter_module_signals.description: Apply pulse for the command limiter when a response is validated.

inter_module_signals.name: command_clamped_out
inter_module_signals.description: Clamp event indication reported to firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: last_request_tag_out
inter_module_signals.description: Last/current request tag presented to firmware.

inter_module_signals.name: accepted_response_count_sig
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted-response counter readback reflected in firmware status.

inter_module_signals.name: rejected_response_count_sig
inter_module_signals.description: Rejected-response counter readback reflected in firmware status.

registers.name: CONTROL
registers.description: Control register with start, abort, enable, and clear_faults bits.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Writing 1 initiates a new request when idle.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enables closed-loop operation and request generation.

fields.name: clear_faults
fields.description: Clears latched faults when written with 1.

fields.name: sequence_seed
fields.description: Seed or next sequence tag used for request framing.

fields.name: timeout_threshold
fields.description: Timeout threshold in clock cycles or implementation-defined tick units.

registers.name: LAST_TAGS
registers.description: Last request and last response tags.

registers.name: SAFE_STATE
registers.description: Safe-state configuration metadata required by firmware contract.

fields.name: safe_state_cfg
fields.description: Documented safe-state selector or metadata word.
